facts.raw_span: A 66-year-old man presented with a 24-hour history of incomplete closure of the right eye
flattening of the right nasolabial fold
right-sided hemiplegia rendering him unable to sit up or stand
Effacement of the right frontal wrinkle
Incomplete closure of the right eyelid
Muscle strength in the right upper and lower extremities: grade 0/5
Hypoesthesia noted on the right side
Right Babinski sign: positive
Emergency CT scan of the head: Hemorrhage in the left thalamus-radiation crown region and in the lateral ventricle at 24 hours postonset

Cerebral MRI with susceptibility-weighted imaging (1 week and 1 month after onset): No definitive lesions in the brainstem or evidence of hemorrhage-related iron deposition in the ventral part of the pons
Cerebral MRI with diffusion tensor imaging (1 month after onset): Corticobulbar tract appeared thinner on the left side than on the right before entering the brainstem
The patient had a 3-year history of hypertension
